claim.why_it_matters: A heading at the wrong level (or none) misplaces the clause in the outline that page_workunit, citation and section lookups read, so the clause is attributed to the wrong parent or not found as a section.
claim.pdf_says: 6.4.2.2 Compiler Directing Statements and Compiler Directing Sentences
claim.markdown_says: ### 6.4.2.2 Compiler Directing Statements and Compiler Directing Sentences
claim.note: Heading at the wrong level: the transcription's convention is one '#' per numbering component (7. is '#', 7.1 '##', 6.4.1 '###', 6.4.2.1 '####', 6.4.2.1.1 '#####'); its sibling 6.4.2.1 is '####' on page 183, so this should be '####' (as '###' it reads as a peer of 6.4.2).

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 184 (IV-38) shows the heading '6.4.2.2 Compiler Directing Statements and Compiler Directing Sentences' in the same style as its sibling 6.4.2.1.2 and children 6.4.2.2.1/6.4.2.2.2; its four-component number makes it a child of 6.4.2 and a sibling of 6.4.2.1. The transcription renders it '### 6.4.2.2' (specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md line 7683) while 6.4.2 is '###' (line 7623) and 6.4.2.1 is '####' (line 7629), so the markdown outline makes 6.4.2.2 a peer of 6.4.2 instead of its child. The text is quoted correctly; only the heading level is wrong, which is a genuine structural defect for outline-based section lookup. Siblings in the same run are also one level short (6.4.2.1.2 '####', 6.4.2.2.1/6.4.2.2.2 '####', 6.4.2.3 '###' and its children) and likely belong to the same sweep.
verdict.corrected_description: Heading 6.4.2.2 is '###' in the transcription; by the transcription's one-'#'-per-component convention and its sibling 6.4.2.1 ('####'), it should be '####'. Its subsections 6.4.2.2.1 and 6.4.2.2.2 (both '####') should likewise be '#####'.
